extra_misconceptions.fact: Paper dust masks trap only solid airborne particulates; solvent vapors require strong cross-ventilation or an organic vapor cartridge.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A paper dust mask filters out toxic organic solvent vapors released by enamel paints, cyanoacrylate glues, and liquid styrene cement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dull blades bind in wood grain and slip unpredictably under heavy force, whereas a sharp blade slices cleanly with light, controlled passes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying heavier downward pressure on a dull #11 hobby blade cuts dense basswood more safely than installing a fresh sharp blade.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Liquid 3D printing resin is a skin sensitizer and aquatic toxin that must be washed in alcohol and cured under UV light before disposal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Uncured photopolymer resin from a stereolithography 3D printer can be washed down a household sink using warm water and dish soap.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Oil-soaked rags generate exothermic heat as they oxidize and can spontaneously ignite unless dried flat outdoors or sealed in a metal can.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Crumpled rags soaked with linseed oil or paint thinner can be tossed directly into an open plastic wastebasket after finishing a model.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to snap off a dull hobby knife blade with bare fingers instead of using pliers and a sharps container?
What distinguishes a standard N95 particulate dust mask from an organic vapor cartridge respirator when spraying solvent lacquer?
Which physical indicator confirms that a spray booth or 3D printer enclosure is exhausting fumes away from your breathing zone?
Where should a Scout position the non-cutting hand relative to the blade travel path when trimming balsa along a steel ruler?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Architectural models visualize spatial aesthetics and site flow, while structural models test load paths, truss deflection, and joint stress.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Architectural models and structural models serve the exact same purpose of showing exterior facade colors and landscaping layouts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Polystyrene solvent cement chemically melts and welds only styrene plastics; non-porous metals, resin, and wood require epoxy or CA glue.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Solvent-based polystyrene cement glues balsa wood, brass rods, and cast resin parts together by filling gaps between their surfaces.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Balsa is ultra-light with coarse pores suited for low-weight frames, whereas basswood has a tight, dense grain that holds crisp machined edges.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Balsa wood and basswood have identical grain density, making them interchangeable for fine structural framing and heavy load tests.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mechanical models test moving kinematic linkages and gears, while process models map piping, valves, and material flow through a facility.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Process models are built purely to test moving gears and linkages rather than the sequence of chemical or manufacturing plant flows.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes the primary engineering purpose of a load-bearing structural model from an exterior architectural site model?
What happens to the bending strength of a balsa wood beam when you slice the strip across the grain instead of parallel to it?
What measurement confirms which candidate sheet material deflects the least when loaded across an identical test span?
Under what condition does solvent-based plastic cement fail to bond two model parts compared to cyanoacrylate or epoxy adhesive?

extra_misconceptions.fact: In a fractional scale ratio, a larger denominator means greater reduction, so a 1:48 model is half the linear size of a 1:24 scale model.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A 1:48 scale model is twice as large in linear dimensions as a 1:24 scale model of the exact same full-size aircraft or building.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pre-made kits are prohibited for this project; the Scout must draft original scaled plans and fabricate the model from raw materials.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modifying or repainting a commercial plastic injection-molded kit satisfies the original design planning rule for Requirement 3.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Perspective sketches foreshorten angles and lengths; accurate part layout requires scaled orthographic front, top, and side projections.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A single perspective sketch provides all the dimensional measurements needed to cut framing members accurately during construction.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Linear dimensions scale by a factor of two, surface area scales by four, and volume or material weight scales by a factor of eight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Doubling the linear scale of a solid model from 1:50 to 1:25 requires only twice as much casting resin or 3D printer filament.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must your orthographic drawing align the front, top, and side views along shared projection lines before you cut any stock?
Which scale ratio produces a physically larger tabletop model of the same building: a 1:24 scale plan or a 1:48 scale plan?
What measurement confirms that your bill of materials includes enough extra linear stock to account for saw kerf and miter cuts?
What happens to interior detail accessibility if your assembly sequence glues the roof or hull closed before painting the cabin?

extra_misconceptions.fact: High helix friction makes most single-start worm drives self-locking, meaning the worm turns the gear wheel but the gear cannot back-drive.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Driving the gear wheel in a worm gear assembly easily spins the worm shaft backward to act as a speed-multiplying overdrive.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Foundry and mold patterns require a slight taper called a draft angle on vertical walls so the pattern releases cleanly from the mold.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An industrial casting pattern with vertical 90-degree sides pulls cleanly out of packed molding sand without tearing the cavity.

extra_misconceptions.fact: End-grain butt joints have minimal glue surface area and peel apart easily unless reinforced with overlapping plywood or cardstock gussets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Butt-gluing balsa bridge truss joints end-to-end without gusset plates provides full tensile and shear strength under test loads.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A four-sided frame with equal opposite sides can still skew into a parallelogram; only equal corner-to-corner diagonals confirm squareness.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Equal opposite wall lengths guarantee that a rectangular architectural floor frame is square without checking diagonal measurements.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a sand or silicone mold when you pull out an industrial casting pattern that has zero draft angle on its walls?
What distinguishes the self-locking torque behavior of a worm gear drive from a reversible spur or lantern gear mechanism?
What measurement confirms that an architectural wall frame or structural bridge truss is truly square before the glue cures?
Where should a Scout position air vents and pouring gates on a two-part mold to prevent trapped air pockets during a casting pour?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Glossy surfaces create broad specular highlights that betray miniature toy scale, so film models use flat matte coats and subtle weathering.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: High-gloss paint makes a small special-effects spacecraft miniature look realistic and massive under bright studio camera lights.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective studio models balance dense mechanical detail areas against smooth hull plating so the human eye can read the ship's silhouette.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Covering every square inch of a spacecraft hull with random dense greebles makes the vessel look more believable on camera.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Consistent scale across crew hatches, docking rings, and thrusters anchors the viewer's perception of the vessel's size in every shot.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A fantasy spacecraft needs no consistent scale ratio because science-fiction vehicles do not exist in the real physical world.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Filming miniatures require an internal rigid brass or aluminum armature anchored to the model's center of gravity to prevent flexing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Camera mounting pylons can be glued directly onto thin exterior styrene hull skins after the spacecraft assembly is completed.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator on a studio miniature gives the camera viewer a clear sense of massive scale during a close-up pass?
What distinguishes the way matte paint finishes scatter studio key lights compared to high-gloss enamel on a small film miniature?
What measurement confirms that your spacecraft's internal mounting point aligns with its center of gravity on a camera pylon?
Under what condition does sealing internal fiber-optic or incandescent lighting inside a closed styrene hull warp the plastic?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Design firms, medical device teams, and architects still rely on physical prototypes to validate ergonomics, acoustics, and spatial feel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Computer-aided 3D rendering has completely eliminated the career role of physical prototype and architectural model makers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many CAD technicians, CNC machinists, and shop modelmakers launch careers through two-year technical degrees, certificates, or apprenticeships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in model fabrication and CAD drafting requires a four-year university degree before you can enter the workforce.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hiring managers value process documentation that shows scaled drawings, iterative material tests, and how the designer solved build errors.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A professional modelmaker's portfolio should display only finished glamour photographs and hide rough sketches or failed test jigs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouting youth protection rules require parent or guardian permission before conducting any internet research or professional interview.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Scout may independently contact and interview an online industrial designer without getting parent or guardian permission first.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms whether an accredited industrial design or engineering degree program fits your long-term tuition budget?
What distinguishes the daily deliverables of an industrial product designer from those of a structural finite-element analyst?
Which physical indicator in a candidate's design portfolio proves mastery of both digital CAD modeling and hands-on shop fabrication?
Under what condition does a Scout have proper authorization to conduct a career research interview with a professional modelmaker?
